pr_title: storagetm: ensure we pass dev_t* to sd_device_get_devnum
pr_body:
On MIPS32 OABI, st_rdev is unsigned long, not dev_t. Use a temporary variable to avoid an incompatible pointer.

Bug: https://bugs.gentoo.org/920576
Fixes: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/30626

review_comments:
man, this mips abi is total garbage, can't the porters who care about this arch get this fixed properly? it's such a mess that this is carried on year over year and has to be patched in myriad of codebases and not a the actual place that caused this mess...

Anyway, please add an explicit comment here somewhere that explains why this indirection is done here, otherwise this will break again once somebody later sees this and decides it's an unnecessary complication that can be dropped, without the context.

Also, please link the relevant MIPS glibc bug report, so that people know where to check to see if things changed and this hack can be dropped again.
Added a comment at both places.
dev_t and st_rdev have different sizes on MIPS32 OABI, so that assert and cast would be counter-productive.
We could add a runtime assert to ensure that the devnum value will fit in st_rdev. But I'm not really sure if that's needed?

Oh, then, does the fix really work??
We push `NvmeSubsystem` object to `Context.subsystems` hashmap with `struct stat` of the device node obtained by `fstat()` as the key.
But when finding the object, we construct a key by `sd_device_get_devnum()`...

I really have no clue how to test if it "really works". This is not a systemd component I am familiar with and I don't have a MIPS system to test on myself.

I think it should work fine so long as sd_device_get_devnum never gives us a device number that exceeds ULONG_MAX (4294967295).

From bits/sysmacros.h in glibc:
```
/* dev_t in glibc is a 64-bit quantity, with 32-bit major and minor numbers.
   Our default encoding is MMMM Mmmm mmmM MMmm, where M is a hex digit of
   the major number and m is a hex digit of the minor number.  This is
   downward compatible with legacy systems where dev_t is 16 bits wide,
   encoded as MMmm.  It is also downward compatible with the Linux kernel,
   which (as of 2016) uses 32-bit dev_t, encoded as mmmM MMmm.

   Systems that use an incompatible encoding for dev_t should override this
   file in the appropriate sysdeps subdirectory.  */
```
Assuming the kernel still only uses 32-bit device numbers, it should be safe to ignore the upper 32-bits of a 64-bit dev_t value.

> Assuming the kernel still only uses 32-bit device numbers, it should be safe to ignore the upper 32-bits of a 64-bit dev_t value.

OK. I agree with that. Thanks.
